svg.aria-label: Authenticated encryption: a message, key and nonce go into ChaCha20-Poly1305, producing ciphertext and a tag; tampering makes decryption fail
svg.text: Meet me at the old oak…

g.text: Eve flips one bit of the ciphertext. When Bob opens it:
“authentication failed”: nothing is decrypted at all

ol.li: An authenticated cipher does two jobs at once. The ciphertext hides the message. The 16-byte tag proves that the ciphertext, and any unencrypted header sent with it, is exactly what the sender sealed. The nonce must never be reused with the same key, or the one-time pad’s weakness comes back.

Encryption alone doesn’t stop tampering: with a stream cipher, flipping a bit of the ciphertext flips the same bit of the message, and Eve could change “10 pounds” into “90 pounds” without knowing the key. The tag makes any change detectable. (These are real bytes from this chapter’s lab.)

figure.figcaption: Authenticated encryption: secrecy and a seal, in one step.
